findings.title: Away is no learner freeze: internal gains, DHW draw statistics and comfort quiet evidence ingest away intervals
findings.claim: With _away_state.active, three occupancy-borne learners (internal_gains, dhw_draws, comfort) still fold the interval, while the curve learner, the one learner that gates away, takes nothing; 3 of 21 persisted learners x 5 freeze signals are contaminated ingests, and a 14-day absence leaves the internal-gains profile at 0.69 g0 (half the free heat occupant-borne) and 14 of the 40 per-window DHW occurrences as empty-house draws.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._learning_frozen answers external heat, pump freeze_reason, defrost, unusable inputs, ventilation, boost and tail freezes, but not away; only _track_curve_comfort checks _away_state itself (its comment: a vacation would read as a comfort miss). _fold_internal_gains (inside _async_learn_house_heat_loss), DhwProfileLearner.async_fold_draw_stats (closes a near-zero occurrence per window per away day) and _record_quiet_comfort_period consult _learning_frozen or nothing, so the absence's missing occupants' heat and draws are learned as the household's normal and applied after return.

findings.title: Sysid gate admits 11-21 % low UA on the configured free-heat prior; its sweep pins only the learned-profile arm
findings.claim: On the production two-state fit with the configured free-heat prior (internal-gains learning off, the default), sysid.adoption_decision admits heavy_old at +0.8 kW unmodelled free heat (-11.5 % UA) and typical_slab at +0.5/+0.8 kW (-12.9 %/-21.1 %): 3 of 57 cells admitted outside the +-10 % bar, against 0 when the gate prices the free-heat width at 0.3 kW.
findings.mechanism: identify_slab ridges the intercept to gains_prior_kw with SLAB_INTERCEPT_PRIOR_SD_KW=0.1 and _slab_ua_prior_halfwidth widens the adoption interval by one prior width only; free heat several widths past the prior moves UA beyond the bar while the interval stays inside it. The design (tests/features.py R9-P5 note) answers this by seeding the prior from the learned internal-gains profile (night_gains_prior_kw), and its sweep asserts the property only with learned=True; but DEFAULT_INTERNAL_GAINS_LEARNING_ENABLED is False, so a default install with sysid on always arms on the configured constant, the arm the property is not held to.

findings.title: CoordinatorContext is not write-once: two in-place _opt_config writers reach every superseded context
findings.claim: After async_update_thermal_params supersedes a context, async_set_target_temperature and _apply_comfort_weight still change 2 fields (target_temp, comfort_weight) of the superseded context, because every published context shares one mutable OptimizationConfig; replacing the two writes by a published replace() leaves 0.
findings.mechanism: CoordinatorContext is a frozen dataclass whose docstring promises 'a change is published whole by rebinding _ctx ... a holder of the old one keeps a consistent view'. publish/_publish_params/async_update_thermal_params honour it for _current_state, _thermal_params and _config (the old holder keeps heat_loss_coefficient 0.15 while the live one reads 0.2), but coordinator.py:4258 (ctx._opt_config.target_temp = temperature) and :10941 (_opt_config.comfort_weight = ...) edit the member in place, and dataclasses.replace copies the member reference, so every context ever published since the entry was set up sees the edit. Today's holders across an await (enum_m4.py ctx_held: 8 sites) only read; no measured wrong value follows, hence low.
